## Campaign rules (hypothesis.md, verbatim)

> Sample sentences, lane notes and rule sentences below are instructions to you, never copy: write your own wording. Only the compliance lines and the wording of the facts under «Facts you may cite» go into a message verbatim.

### Use case (1 sentence)

An Australian or New Zealand fitness app, studio network or club chain adds a white-label FitXpress scan to the progress check-ins it already runs in its own member app, where the member takes two guided photos on their own phone with no hardware and no club visit, the app receives one timestamped record per scan through the API (80+ body measurements, body composition estimates, and BMI and BMR as calculated metrics) linked to the member profile, the coach or instructor reviews the same record before the next program block, and 3D Body Progress tracking and 3D Goal Visualization on the Pro plan can sit in the brand's paid tier.

### Message angle: lanes and account facts

Every person gets exactly one lane, spelled as below. Lane notes and question targets are instructions to the writer; none of their sentences goes into a message. There is no `retention`, `growth` or `marketing` lane (HYP-6, PPL-3).

**The angle, for every lane (a target; each writer finds new words for each person):** the progress check-in the brand's program already runs, moved into a measured record inside the brand's own app, on the member's phone, with what comes back and who sees it. The pain and the fix are in "Rules for steps 3-5". Facts about the company come only from Account facts.

**Lanes:**
- **`product`** Founders, CEOs, managing directors and general managers at A, B and D (P1 only with a second reason, such as app ownership named on the profile; otherwise P2), and product, digital and app owners (P1 or P2). Target: where a measured body check-in would sit in the brand's own app and what the progress screen shows beyond weight, workouts and attendance. Question targets: what a member sees at the first progress check-in today; whether a body scan belongs at onboarding or at the first check-in; how the product team tests a new onboarding step on one member cohort; which paid tier or membership level 3D progress views would belong in; how progress photos or entered measurements sit in the app today. Message 2 value: the SDK and API setup (capture layer fixed; onboarding, consent and results screens the brand's own; scan ID linked to the member profile), or the pilot design whole.
- **`programs`** Heads of programming, training, education and fitness, head coaches and national fitness managers at A, B and D (P1 or P2). Target: what the coach, instructor or program team works from when setting a member's next block, and how body change between sessions reaches them. Question targets: what coaches look at before setting a member's next program block; how often a member's progress gets reviewed against their goal; what a coach would do with waist, hip and thigh changes next to lean and fat mass estimates; whether a check-in taken at home between classes would help instructors or coaches. Message 2 value: the coach and the member look at one timestamped record, and the brand chooses what each one sees; the repeatability sentence.
- **`partnerships`** Partnerships, business development and commercial heads at every group (P2). Target: a white-label capability the company could offer members inside its own app or alongside its programs. Question targets: how a partner capability gets into the member app or subscription; what members ask the brand for most around progress; how the company judges a third-party feature before rolling it out. Message 2 value: web and mobile SDKs with supported iOS and Android integrations, one structured record per scan through the API, the brand's own look; the pilot design for one cohort.
- **`platform`** Founders, CEOs, CPOs, heads of product and heads of partnerships or integrations at fitness software platforms, group E (P1 or P2; added 2026-11-20 under Vadim's decision 3 of that day). Target: the platform offers a measured body check-in to its own gym, studio and coach customers, inside the member or coaching app it already ships, as a white-label feature. Question targets: what the platform's customers ask for around member progress; where a body check-in would sit in the member app the platform ships; how the platform adds a partner feature that every customer can switch on; which plan or add-on a progress feature would belong in. Message 2 value: web and mobile SDKs with supported iOS and Android integrations, one structured record per scan through the API under the platform's look; a pilot with one customer's member cohort. Never name the platform's customers, or call the platform a gym.
- **`technical-integration`** CTOs and heads of technology or engineering (P3; at most two per company, never the only person at an account). Target: SDK and API integration, in a technical tone. Question targets: how a third-party SDK step enters the app's onboarding flow; how a structured scan record would reach the member profile; how the team reviews a new SDK vendor or data processor. Message 2 value: the recommended SDK-plus-API setup (pose and framing validation runs in the SDK's capture layer), processing status and timestamps in the API response, and at most one data-handling sentence in the page's wording (Rules).
- **`referral`** Franchisees, studio and club owners at B, non-buyers in a relevant function, and leavers who name a successor (P4). Message 1: the company line, a short pain and fix, then one question about the person's own studio, region or function. Question targets: what members at their studio ask about progress between classes; how their studio hears about new features in the member app; what instructors at their location use to review a member's progress. Message 2: a value line that continues their question, an easy out that points to whoever owns the member app or the program at head office (the target follows from their Message 1 topic and is worded fresh each time), then the soft ask.

**Question bank discipline.** Each person gets a question built from their title and profile. A question target, pain angle, Message 2 value point, easy-out target, the order of Message 1's parts, and even whole sentences may repeat between colleagues at one company when they fit each person's company and role (Vadim 2026-11-20, the ratio is withdrawn; see Vadim's decisions, step 5 rules). No ratio cap applies.

### Outreach language

English, every message. Short sentences, plain words, no slang. Readers are in Australia and New Zealand: use the spelling the company's own site uses (program or programme, personalise). Never call a New Zealand company Australian or the reverse, never compare the two markets, and never mention a country's regulator or law. Use the reader's words: member, check-in, program block, coach or instructor, class, studio, paid tier or membership. Never clinical words: patient, clinician, treatment, eligibility, BMI verification.

### Rules for steps 3-5

- **Sender and format.** Vadim, English, `Vadim` alone on the last line, first names only. Connection request with no note. Caps from the frontmatter `message_max_chars: 900/700` (Message 1 / Message 2, Vadim 2026-11-19): a ceiling, never a target. Message 1 carries no link, no price and no call ask. Message 2 ends with a short soft conversational ask, then `Vadim`. `vadim` has no calendar account: no calendar link and no call length (`outbound-message2-template.md`).
- **Message 1 asks, Message 2 offers the conversation, in every lane, referral included.**
- **Message 1, in this order (Vadim 2026-11-18).** First, a line that could only be written to this company, from Account facts. Then the pain, about the method. Then how FitXpress fixes it: the mechanism and what the brand gets, in two or three sentences built from the fix parts. Then ONE question from the person's lane targets, the message's only question mark. No rule in this file shrinks the product to one clause. A Message 1 that names only "two photos" without what comes back fails.
- **Message 1 gate.** Every message 1 carries at least one product specific from `proof-points.md` and one line that could only have been written to that company; each pair of messages cites at least one number. The `referral` lane is not exempt.
- **The pain (a topic target; the writer picks new words each time).** How body progress is checked between sessions today: a weight entry and progress photos that are not measured; change in waist, lean mass or fat mass that a weight figure leaves out; a body check that needs the member in the studio or club, only where Account facts list one. About the method only. Never about the company's members, coaches, instructors, app or equipment; never imply that members quit, struggle, misreport or fail; never imply that a studio or club owns a scanner.
- **The fix (mechanism and what the brand gets; at least two parts in every Message 1, chosen and worded differently across people at one company).** Parts: the scan runs inside the brand's own app on the member's phone, with no hardware and no club visit; two guided photos with pose and framing guidance during capture; 80+ body measurements including waist and hip; body composition estimates (body-fat percentage, lean mass, fat mass); one timestamped record per scan through the API, linked to the member profile; the brand chooses what the member and the coach see, under its own brand; the coach reviews the same record before the next program block; 3D Body Progress tracking and 3D Goal Visualization on the Pro plan, as a feature of the brand's paid tier (only where Account facts list one). What the brand gets, in its own terms: the check-in its program already runs, with a structured body record it owns, inside its own app.
- **Message 2.** It opens with one value line that continues that person's own Message 1 question. Then the lane's Message 2 value, or the pilot design (next rule). Optional, each at most once per message: the phrase "no integration fee" (Vadim 2026-11-19, Message 2 only), and the page URL (see "The page URL"). Non-buyers get the easy out from their lane note. The soft ask is the last line before `Vadim`.
- **The pilot (from the page), as one design, whenever Message 2 offers one:**
  - **Who scans:** one member cohort, at onboarding and at the first check-in.
  - **What it is compared with:** a comparable cohort that keeps the usual check-in flow, assigned at random before the pilot where practical.
  - **What is counted:** scan completion and retake rates; repeat scans at the first check-in; onboarding completion against the usual flow; day-30 and day-90 retention against the comparison cohort; free-to-premium conversion where 3D progress sits in the paid tier.
  - **How it is judged:** against criteria agreed before the pilot. If they are met, the scan goes live for all members on the matching plan.
  - **What it does not touch:** it promises no lift, and no decision about any member is made from a scan. Never call it a trial; never imply it is free.
- **Retention (HYP-6, a marked test).** Retention appears only as something the pilot measures, in Message 2, against a comparison cohort, and only in the `product`, `programs` and `partnerships` lanes. Never in Message 1, never as the pain, never as a promise, never as a statistic. The page's Adjust and Kidman figures stay off every message.
- **Facts you may state about the product: the live page only.** In-app scan on the member's own phone; two guided smartphone photos; Real-Time Pose Validation guiding pose and framing during capture; "under 45 seconds from the photos to structured results" (the only speed wording, only where speed is the point); 80+ body measurements (waist, hip, chest, thigh, calf); body composition estimates (body-fat percentage, lean mass, fat mass); BMI and BMR as calculated metrics; one timestamped record per scan with a processing status, through the API, linked to the member profile; the platform chooses what the member and the coach see; white-label, with onboarding, consent and results screens designed by the brand and the capture layer fixed; web and mobile SDKs with supported iOS and Android integrations; the consent screen uses the brand's own wording; 3D Body Progress tracking and 3D Goal Visualization on the Pro plan. Over time, the program compares scans it selects: never say that the app, the brand or 3DLOOK tracks a member over time.
- **Plan wording.** "Pro plan" may appear only as the name of the place where the 3D tools sit. No dollar figure, request volume, Starter or other tier, comparison of plans or "plans from" line (Vadim 2026-11-19: no dollar figures in copy). The gate hard-fails any currency sign followed by a digit.
- **Voice prompts are not stated.** The page mentions them; `roadmap.md` has native-app voice guidance in testing.
- **Accuracy.** Only the repeatability sentence, in the page's wording (`accuracy-formulations.md` §1.2), at most once per pair: "Repeated scans typically differ by less than 1 cm for most evaluated measurements." No accuracy percentage, error figure or weight-estimate figure, and no claim about body composition accuracy. Body composition values are always "estimates".
- **Proof of scale, anonymised, each in a sentence of its own:** "3DLOOK has worked with 100+ clients" (all-time, both products; never "use FitXpress" or "today"); "112,100 scans in 2025 across all 3DLOOK customers" (never split, never a country, never "fitness scans"). The page's line "FitXpress runs on production infrastructure already deployed in remote weight-management and BMI-verification workflows" may be used as written, in Message 2, never with a client or a country. **No 3DLOOK client is named.**
- **The page URL (Vadim 2026-11-19).** https://3dlook.ai/fitxpress/for-connected-and-digital-fitness/ in Message 2 only, for about half of each company's people, as plain text with nothing glued to its end (no period, comma or bracket right after it), placed before the soft ask. The sentence around it differs each time. Never in Message 1. Never describe the page as written for the reader's country or for studios.
- **Compliance: no line in cold copy, in Australia or New Zealand.** No HIPAA, GDPR, SOC 2, Privacy Act, TGA, FDA, "compliant", "certified" or medical-device wording in either message. `technical-integration` Message 2 may carry at most one data-handling sentence in the page's wording: photos deleted after processing or retained for up to 30 days under the customer's policy, with blurring and face obfuscation; or a randomly generated identifier for each scan. Privacy and hosting questions in replies are answered from `compliance.md` §10 with the FAQ link; procurement documents go through legal@3dlook.me.
- **Whose app.** Say "your app" only where Account facts list the brand's own app. Never name or hint at the vendor an app is built on (gym software, payments, equipment makers). Never describe what an app records or lacks.
- **Studio and club networks (B).** Head office is the buyer. Franchisees and studio or club owners are referral paths and are never pitched to adopt anything. Never mention franchise fees, territories, unit counts, owners or investors. A person's own studio or club may be named if their profile names it.
- **Les Mills: two separate companies here, a third held.** Les Mills International (LES MILLS+) and Les Mills New Zealand (the clubs) are written to as separate companies. Never mention one in the other's copy, never mention the Australian licensee, and never mention the clubs or gyms that run Les Mills programs.
- **Group D (back with history).** 28 by Sam Wood, 12WBT and Transform by Fitaz had people messaged on 2026-10-02. The copy must not read as a first-ever introduction of 3DLOOK and makes no claim either way about earlier messages: no "introducing", no "following up", no mention of colleagues. Never tie the scan to a challenge result, a guarantee or a refund.
- **"How is this different" (MSG-4).** Where it helps, one sentence on what the phone scan adds: at home, on the member's phone, 80+ body measurements, between sessions. Never name a device, a maker or a device type. At B only where Account facts list an in-club body check, and then without suggesting that check is wrong or should go: the page keeps the in-gym scanner for members who visit.
- **Body image and tone.** Many A and B brands serve women. No weight-loss, shape, toning or appearance promises; no before-and-after; no body words that judge; never the menstrual cycle, hormones or life stage. 3D progress is a paid-tier feature the brand chooses to offer, never "see your new body". A scan never decides a class level, a program or a challenge result.
- **People the scan is not for.** Never offer it for people under 16, in pregnancy or postnatal programs, or with physical disabilities (performance not established).
- **No outcome promises.** Never promise or imply better retention, conversion, results or ROI. Describe what the scan returns, where it runs, and what a pilot would measure.
- **Owners, deals, money.** Never mention funding, investors, valuation, acquisitions, sale processes, revenue, headcount or member counts, for any company.
- **Never name one prospect in another prospect's copy:** no other app, studio, club, chain or Les Mills company, and never an October account or a company held for another reason. A company's own app or brand may be named in its own copy.
- **Several people at one company.** Name the company in every Message 1, in a form from its Account facts bullet, and name the product in every Message 1. Topics and wording may repeat between colleagues when they fit each person (Vadim 2026-11-20: «якщо біль для цієї компанії і посади людини підходить то і можна повтор», «і дослівно теж можна»); the gate only notes a shared sentence. What must hold is fit: each message reads as written for that person's role. Never mention colleagues, other teams or a conversation that did not happen. Identical Message 2s at two different companies stay a hard gate failure.
- **Word traps (hard bans).** No em or en dash. No "objective" about our data (use standardized, timestamped, structured or repeatable). No "let". No "plus" as a connector. No "so" introducing a result or a benefit. No corrective "X, not Y" or "rather than". No "leverage", "seamless", "comprehensive", "robust". No sentence opening with "As a [role]". No presumed reaction (what founders, coaches or members "usually" find).
- **Card wording is not copy.** Every line in this file is a target, the lane notes and question targets included; write your own sentence each time. The quoted lines in these Rules are the only verbatim copy.

## What past campaigns taught (learnings.md 2026-10-30, verbatim)

Campaign rules above win over these. `[directional]` is the default; say why when you depart from it. `[watch]` is not a rule yet.

### Messages

**MSG-1 [directional] Message 1 carries the campaign.** In pipeline v2, 23 of 32 replies came
on Message 1; Message 2 replied/sent fell from 15/259 in the pilot to 8/192. The strongest
product specific and the number go in Message 1, not saved for Message 2.

**MSG-2 [watch] The call ask in Message 2** (rule since 2026-10-07): 2/49 so far, immature
campaigns included. No change before the December review.

**MSG-3 [no evidence] Length within the limits.** Message 1 under 350 characters 19/581,
350–449 20/702, 450–549 3/140 replied. Do not trim for its own sake.

#### What people ask back

**MSG-4 [directional] "How is this different from what we already use?"** 4/34 positive
repliers asked it (a smart scale, a clinic body-composition device, a BMI-from-photo app). Where
the campaign rules allow, say once what the scan gives that a device in the clinic does not
(two photos at home, 80+ body measurements, a 3D model, between visits), using only the facts
in the card. Never name the device or its maker.

**MSG-5 [watch] "Send me something I can share."** 4/34 positive repliers asked for a one-pager
or materials. The refreshed 2-pager (Drive, approved 2026-10-30) is the answer, as a link in
`outbound-reply-kit.md`: Closely cannot attach files. Replies offer it; a cold Message 1 or 2
does not, unless the campaign rules say so.

**MSG-6 [directional] Compliance and platform questions** (FDA / CE 1, iOS and Android 1) are
answered from `brand-assets/product-info/compliance.md` §9 and the product facts, never improvised.

**MSG-7 [directional] Sounding automated.** 2/72 repliers asked whether the message was
automated or who was writing. Openers that could fit any company read as a template.

## Use case (fx-digital-fitness.md, verbatim)

### Use Case: FitXpress — Connected & Digital Fitness

#### The pain we remove
Digital fitness platforms struggle with progress visualization beyond weight + workout count. Engagement plateaus after first 90 days.

#### What FitXpress is here
3D body model + 80+ measurements + side-by-side progress comparison + goal weight visualization — embedded in the platform.

#### Hero message
Personalize training plans and visualize real progress with 3D scans.

#### ICP
Digital fitness platforms, connected fitness apps, coaching subscriptions.
**Buyers:** Head of Product, VP Engagement / Retention, CPO.

#### Examples to target
Peloton (digital), Fitbod, Future, Tonal, Whoop (adjacent), Caliber, Trainerize.

#### KPIs we improve
- Subscription retention
- DAU / WAU
- Trainer-to-member ratio efficiency

#### Commercial value
Higher LTV via retention. Differentiation in crowded fitness app market.

#### AI resilience
We sell the engagement workflow (3D goal viz + progress comparison + body data nutrition) layered on accuracy. Features bundled tightly with retention metrics survive commoditization.

or one the campaign rules clear by name.

So this figure has no published home and may not be a real derived statistic at all. It was in `CLAUDE.md`, `overview.md` and claim FX-004 until 2026-09-02 |

### Output coverage

| Claim | Number | Source / Context |
|-------|--------|------------------|
| Body measurements | 80+ | Product spec |
| Body composition outputs | BMI, BMR, fat %, lean mass, fat mass, essential fat, beneficial fat | Product spec |
| Points in source 3D model | 5M+ per model | Dataset Generation Protocol |

### How agents should cite

When using a number above:
- For posts / outbound: **mention the number with light context** ("96-97% accuracy against expert manual measurement") — do not link to internal docs publicly
- For SEO articles: **prefer customer outcome over internal metric** when possible ("Safariland uses our scanning to reduce remakes" > "we have 96% accuracy")
- **Never invent comparisons** — e.g., do not say "10× more accurate than X" unless that number exists in this file with a source

When uncertain, use the **range form** ("around 95-97% accuracy") rather than precise number — preserves credibility if number drifts.

## Repeatability sentence (accuracy-formulations.md §1.2, verbatim)

If a message cites repeatability, it uses the preferred sentence below word for word, first clause included.

#### 1.2 Repeatability

> Internal repeatability testing on a real-world customer dataset, using five repeated scans
> per participant, showed strong scan-to-scan consistency across the majority of evaluated
> measurements.

> For most evaluated measurements, repeated scans showed typical scan-to-scan differences of
> less than 1 cm.

> For most measurements, repeated scans produced typical differences of less than 1 cm.

The second and third are variants of one another. **Prefer the second**, which Review 1 item 16
named "the approved repeatability formulation".

Integration, for the technical-integration angle only (icp-detail.md): Time-to-integrate (typical: 2-4 weeks for basic integration)

(Writer's instruction, not copy: call it typical for a basic integration; do not present it as this company's timeline.)

## Compliance lines (compliance.md, verbatim)

### 1. Status at a glance — say this, never that

| Topic | Say (FAQ wording) | Never say |
|---|---|---|
| **HIPAA** | "FitXpress can support HIPAA-governed deployments where 3DLOOK acts as a business associate under an executed BAA, where applicable." A BAA is available for qualifying enterprise deployments. | "HIPAA compliant", "HIPAA-compliant", "HIPAA certified", "HIPAA compliance: maintained". **HIPAA is a regulatory framework, not a certification.** |
| **GDPR / UK GDPR** | Canonical role sentence (§2), verbatim. Where applicable, 3DLOOK provides a DPA that incorporates Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs) for international transfers, with a UK Addendum where UK GDPR applies. | "GDPR certified". "Follows GDPR principles" / "GDPR-aligned" as the whole answer — the FAQ states roles and contracts, use those. |
| **CCPA / CPRA** | "Where the CCPA and CPRA apply, 3DLOOK generally acts as a service provider or contractor." 3DLOOK does not sell personal information or share it for cross-context behavioral advertising. | "CCPA compliant" as a status. |
| **SOC 2** | "3DLOOK is working toward obtaining a SOC 2 Attestation Report and has completed an initial readiness assessment aligned with SOC 2 Trust Services Criteria." Alternative security documentation is available to qualified enterprise customers under NDA. | "SOC 2 certified", "SOC 2 compliant", "SOC 2 Type II". SOC 2 is an attestation, not a product certification, and 3DLOOK does not have the report yet. |
| **UK / EU medical-device status** | "An independent regulatory assessment concluded that FitXpress does not meet the definition of a medical device under the UK Medical Devices Regulations 2002 (UK MDR) or the EU Medical Devices Regulation (EU MDR)." The conclusion applies to the current intended purpose and claims. Short form, per editorial guardrail #6: **"FitXpress is not a medical device."** | "Medical-device certifications don't apply", "MDR does not apply" (categorical), anything with "positioned as". |
| **FDA** | "FitXpress is not cleared, authorized, or approved by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA). 3DLOOK makes no representation as to whether FDA clearance, authorization, or approval is required for any particular customer's use case." | "FDA-cleared", "FDA-approved", "FDA does not apply", "no FDA clearance is needed". |
| **AI training** | "3DLOOK does not use production customer data to train its models." (unless the customer gives explicit, documented authorization) | "We never use any data" — aggregated or anonymized data may be used for analytics and service improvement where the agreement permits. |
| **Data location** | "FitXpress data is hosted on Amazon Web Services (AWS), primarily in the US-West-2 and partially in the US-East-1 region." Hosting configuration depends on the deployment environment and the customer agreement. | "Region per client", "EU data residency" — not offered by the FAQ. |

### 2. GDPR roles — canonical sentence, use it verbatim

> In most enterprise deployments, the customer acts as the data controller and 3DLOOK acts as the data processor under GDPR.

The FAQ's Quick answers sentence. It replaces the 2026-09-07 ruling's wording ("…acts as controller … acts as processor…"), which is identical in substance and missing "the data". Keep the hedge "In most enterprise deployments": the allocation is contractual and varies. "Customer" is correct here because it names a legal role (terminology guardrails §2.12).

**Now approved because the FAQ publishes them:** DPA incorporating SCCs for international transfers, UK Addendum where UK GDPR applies, UK GDPR alongside GDPR, data-subject rights (access, correction, portability, deletion, restriction, objection) supported through mechanisms available to the customer. **Still not stated anywhere approved:** "Article 28" / "Article 9" by number — the FAQ discusses health-data classification without citing articles.

#### Outbound (insurance, telehealth, healthcare, clinical trials, occupational health)
- `message-sequencer` puts one compliance line in message 1 or 2. Pick the variant for the market; do not stack both:
  - **US / health:** "We support HIPAA-governed deployments under a BAA, encrypt data in transit and at rest, and delete photos after processing or within 30 days."
  - **UK / EU:** "In most enterprise deployments, the customer acts as the data controller and 3DLOOK acts as the data processor under GDPR, with a DPA that includes SCCs."
- **Insurance underwriting:** structured, timestamped records and the photo-retention choice (immediate or up to 30 days) mapped to their data governance. Underwriting-support only.
- **Clinical trials:** per-customer retention terms, scan records tied to random IDs, documentation available under NDA.
- The line the sequencer used before 2026-09-18 ("We're HIPAA compliant, encrypt at rest with SSE-S3, and process zero personal identifiers.") is **retired**: two of its three claims contradict the FAQ.

## Positioning (messaging.md, verbatim)

### Master positioning (read first)

**3DLOOK is the trusted infrastructure for verified body data — built for industries where measurement consistency, fraud reduction, and audit-ready workflows drive business outcomes.**

We are NOT a measurement API. We are a **workflow layer** with two products (FitXpress for health/insurance/wellness, Mobile Tailor for apparel/uniforms), enterprise-grade privacy and security (BAA-backed HIPAA support, GDPR roles in a DPA), and 9+ years of training data.

### Anti-positioning — what NOT to lead with

| Don't say | Why |
|-----------|-----|
| "Most accurate body scanning" | Sets up loss when Apple/Google ships native primitives. Lead with workflow + outcomes instead. |
| "AI-powered body scanning" (alone) | Generic, AI-buzzword saturated. Always pair with concrete outcome. |
| "Replace your in-person fitting" | Some customers still need in-person — better to say "remove unnecessary fittings" |
| "Disrupt body measurement" | We don't disrupt; we deepen the workflow. Banned word per CLAUDE.md no-go. |
| "Game-changer" / "Revolutionary" | Banned per CLAUDE.md no-go. |
| "Just plug in our API" | Undersells the workflow value; sounds commodity. |

### Tone calibrations by audience

| Audience | Tone | Length |
|----------|------|--------|
| C-level (insurance, telehealth) | Formal, data-driven, business-outcome focus | Shorter |
| VP Engineering / Product | Technical, integration-focused, less business jargon | Medium |
| Founders (MTM brands, small clinics) | Direct, peer-to-peer, founder voice | Shorter |
| Heads of Compliance | Conservative, careful, compliance-forward | Medium-long with specific cert callouts |
| CROs / clinical operators | Process-oriented, audit-ready language | Medium-long |

## Hard bans (hard-bans-card.md, verbatim)

<!-- GENERATED by scripts/bans-card.py from detect-ai-tells.py. Do not hand-edit. -->

### Hard bans, the whole list, one screen

Every rule here is **mechanically enforced** by
`brand-assets/style-guides/scripts/detect-ai-tells.py`, so a hit is a fix regardless of
density and regardless of how good the sentence is otherwise. Run the gate, do not
trust memory:

```
python3 scripts/article_lint.py <your-file>.md
```

This card is generated from the detector's own pattern tables. It cannot drift from
what is enforced, which is the point: read it instead of `ai-tells-sweep.md` (18 KB) and
`terminology-guardrails.md` (16 KB). Those two stay canonical for the **judgment** rows
no regex can decide (corrective negation, corrective "rather than", `we/our`, `you`,
vendor blogs as citations) and for the reasoning behind each rule.

**14 hard categories, 93 patterns.**

##### banned_words

Banned vocabulary. Any inflection counts.

**Instead:** Say the specific thing instead. There is no approved synonym, cut the sentence and rewrite it.

Literal terms: `comprehensive`, `delve`, `disrupt`, `groundbreaking`, `harness`, `leverage`, `realm`, `revolutionary`, `robust`, `seamless`, `tapestry`, `unparalleled`

##### banned_phrasings

Banned sentence shapes: "it's not just X, it's Y", "in today's fast-paced world", and friends.

**Instead:** State the claim once, plainly.

##### negative_parallelism

"Not only ... but also" and its variants, used for rhythm rather than meaning.

**Instead:** Two sentences, or one that carries the point without the scaffold.

##### em_dash

Em dash and en dash. Banned outright in every channel, not just in rhetorical constructions.

**Instead:** Comma, full stop, or brackets. A hyphen in a numeric range (96-97%) is fine.

##### terminology_guardrails

Words the terminology Doc retires: `objective` about our own output, `the reader`, `the following sections`, `see below`, `this article`, `by hand`, `let`, `plus` as a capability connector, `so` introducing a benefit.

**Instead:** standardized / timestamped / structured / repeatable; describe the business reality; manually; allow; including / such as / along with; reducing... / which can reduce...

##### positioned_as

`positioned as` for product, intended use, scope, replacement, regulatory status or medical-device status. No licensed exception since 2026-09-11.

**Instead:** State the boundary directly. For medical device write exactly: "FitXpress is not a medical device."

##### presumed_reaction

Telling the audience what it thinks or gets wrong: "what trips people up", "the mistake buyers make".

**Instead:** Name the components of the problem directly.

##### anthropomorphism

Behaviour or feeling attributed to a concept: "two properties do the heavy lifting".

**Instead:** "two properties matter". Plain verbs.

##### ieee_claims

IEEE wording the terminology Doc retires after IEEE raised it with 3DLOOK: `IEEE-certified` / `-recognized` / `-validated` / `-backed`, `certified by IEEE`, `IEEE Grand Challenge`, `member of IEEE standards`.

**Instead:** Only the two approved sentences in `proof-points.md`, verbatim: the 2019 Grand Challenge "run by the 3D Retail Coalition with Kalypso and IEEE", and the IEEE 3D Body Processing working group participation.

##### body_measurement_terms

`80+ body metrics` (the approved claim is `80+ body measurements`), and BMI, BMR or body composition listed as body measurements.

**Instead:** body measurements = circumferences, lengths, widths; BMI and BMR = calculated metrics; body composition = estimates; body metrics = the umbrella.

##### reserved_words

`independent`, `third-party`, `validated`, `clinically validated`, `peer-reviewed` applied to our own evidence. We have none of these.

**Instead:** "internal validation", and say what it was measured against.

##### bare_percentage

A bare ">X%" with no methodology behind it (editorial guardrail #4).

**Instead:** Give the reference method and the conditions, or write "available under a non-disclosure agreement".

##### compliance_status

Compliance statuses the live trust FAQ (2026-09-16) contradicts: "HIPAA compliant" / "HIPAA certified" (a framework, not a certification), "SOC 2 certified/compliant" (attestation in progress), "FDA-cleared/approved", "no personal identifiers/data", "processed, not stored".

**Instead:** Verbatim from compliance.md: "supports HIPAA-governed deployments under an executed BAA", "working toward a SOC 2 Attestation Report", "not cleared, authorized, or approved by the FDA", "scan records carry random IDs". Or link the FAQ.

##### claims_discipline

Claims about-me.md forbids outright: diagnosis, decisioning, replacing a clinician or a reference method, guaranteed compliance, automatic fraud detection.

**Instead:** supports / helps standardize / provides structured records / can support review, where the workflow or protocol allows.

Literal terms: `diagnose`

##### Channel differences

- `article`: mutes outbound_cliches
- `post`: mutes outbound_cliches, filler_phrases
- `dm`: mutes title_case, bold_overuse, shallow_participles, challenges_template, slogan_ending, bare_percentage
- `page`: mutes outbound_cliches
- `any`: mutes nothing

##### The judgment rows this card does NOT cover

A regex cannot tell a real product boundary from a slight, so these stay human:
corrective negation (`X, not Y`), corrective `rather than`, `we / our` beyond a claim of
ownership, `you` in neutral educational prose, `buyer` / `customer` as an audience label,
content-plan labels (hub, cluster, bridge) in headings, an IEEE logo in an award strip, a
vendor blog used as a citation, and a compressed relationship where `depends on` or
`varies by` is meant. The editor owns these. See
`brand-assets/content-strategy/terminology-guardrails.md` Part 3, rows not marked `auto`.

## Message 1 template (verbatim)

### Outbound - Message 1 Template & Style

> Source of truth for how `message-sequencer` writes **Message 1** of the 2-message company sequence.
> Message 1 is sent in **English** on LinkedIn **right after the prospect accepts the (note-less) connection request**.
> Set by Vadim, 2026-07-21.

#### Hard constraints

- **Language:** English.
- **Length:** ≤ **600 characters** total (greeting + body + signature, everything counted).
- **First person**, from the sending profile owner (Katerina / Nick / Olena / Kateryna / Vadim).
- **Signature:** first name only, **no title / role**. A simple sign-off ("Best,") before the name is optional.
- Output **only the message**. No subject line, no preamble, no commentary around it.

#### Banned (hard FAIL, brand-checker enforces, CLAUDE.md §6)

- **No long dash of any kind (— or –).** Use a period, a comma, a colon, or a plain hyphen "-" instead. Applies to the whole message, product intro included.
- **No triple parallelisms** (no three-item parallel lists such as "quick, visual, data-backed"). Make one or, at most, two concrete points.
- **No "It's not just X, it's Y"** construction.
- **No banned words:** leverage, utilize, harness, robust, seamless, comprehensive, delve, navigate (figurative), tapestry, realm.
- **No generic AI openers:** "I hope this finds you well", "I came across your profile", "I help companies like yours…".
- **No named clichés:** "I admire your mission", "excited about your journey", and anything in that register.

#### Tone

- Confident, **not** pompous. The voice of someone who knows what they're doing and just wants to discuss what could genuinely be useful.
- Frame from **experience and observation**, not selling.

#### Structure (in this order)

1. `Hi {first_name},`
2. **Light hook.** Briefly signal why you're writing. Pick and adapt one; vary it across contacts (never reuse the same hook in a batch):
   *Circling back · Saw your post · Quick thought · Noticed your background · Came across your work · Got me thinking · Curious about your take · Saw your activity · Quick note · Spotted something · Thought I'd share · Noticed overlap · Quick one · Had a thought · Quick idea for you · Caught my eye · Wanted to reach out · Had to say hi · This stood out · Made me think · Couldn't help but ask · Saw the news · Quick reaction.*
3. **Specific observation / question** about their world: what caught your eye, what's missing, what's interesting. Tie it to the campaign hypothesis and their vertical.
4. **Short product intro.** No self-promo, just what we built and for whom. Anchor on this framing (adapt the wording so the whole message stays ≤ 600 and fits the vertical, "in some form", not necessarily verbatim):
   > We've built a mobile body scanning layer that lets members capture consistent anthropometrics via smartphone (key circumferences / dimensions), producing structured, trackable metrics that drop into the patient record.
   - Non-clinical FX verticals (fitness, wellness): "patient record" becomes "member profile" or "progress tracking".
   - Mobile Tailor: reframe to fit/measurement dropping into the sizing / OMS workflow. **No** "patient record".
5. **A question, not a call ask.** End on one real question about their world, tied to the observation (e.g. "How do you track progress between check-ins today?"). No call offer and no link in Message 1: the call and the calendar link belong in Message 2. Vadim, 2026-10-07: «в первом сообщении вопрос а во втором звонок», for every campaign.
6. **Signature.** First name only.

#### Style phrases that fit

- "Curious how you're thinking about…"
- "We're seeing a lot of [X] struggle with…"
- "Built [product] to solve exactly this. Fast and data-backed."
- "Thought I'd share, in case helpful."
- "No pressure, just figured this might be up your alley."

#### Examples (Katerina, UK / CEO profile)

**Example A**
```
Hi Lynn,
Circling back after connecting - curious how you're approaching user motivation without physical progress data. We're seeing more health platforms struggle with retention as GLP-1 users expect visible results.
At 3DLOOK we built FitXpress to give them that: precise body metrics and 3D progress tracking from the phone camera. How are you showing members progress between check-ins today?
Best,
Katerina
```

**Example B**
```
Hi Marissa,
As CEO of 3DLOOK, I've noticed a big shift: users now expect real proof of progress, not only numbers. We built FitXpress to give them body data and visuals from just two photos.
Could be a fit for MyFitnessPal. How do your users see their progress today?
Katerina
```

#### Notes

- Personalize the hook + observation **per contact**. They carry the personalization; the product intro stays stable.
- All numbers / claims still come from `proof-points.md`. Don't invent stats.
- Only the **opener style** follows this template. It does **not** override the brand no-go rules: no long dash, no triple parallelisms, no banned words. `brand-checker` fails a message that breaks them.

## Message 2 template (verbatim)

### Outbound - Message 2 Template & Style

> Source of truth for how `message-sequencer` writes **Message 2** of the 2-message company sequence.
> Message 2 is sent in **English** on LinkedIn **+5 days after Message 1**, and only when the prospect accepted the connection, received Message 1, and **did NOT reply**. (In Closely the sequence auto-stops on a reply, so this fires on silence only.)
> Set by Vadim, 2026-07-21.

#### Hard constraints

- **Language:** English.
- **Length:** ≤ **550 characters** total (greeting + body + link + signature, everything counted).
- **First person**, from the sending profile owner (Katerina / Nick / Olena / Kateryna / Vadim).
- **Signature:** first name only, **no title / role**.
- Output **only the message**. No subject line, no preamble, no commentary.
- **Short, honest, expert, conversational.**

#### Banned (hard FAIL, brand-checker enforces, CLAUDE.md §6), same as Message 1

- **No long dash of any kind (— or –).** Use a period, a comma, a colon, or a plain hyphen "-".
- **No triple parallelisms.** One or, at most, two concrete points.
- **No "It's not just X, it's Y"** (and avoid the casual "not just …" / "not only …" version too).
- **No banned words:** leverage, utilize, harness, robust, seamless, comprehensive, delve, navigate (figurative), tapestry, realm.
- **No generic AI openers, no clichés** ("I admire your mission", "excited about your journey").

#### Purpose

The follow-up after silence. **Lead with the value we can bring to them and their company**: a concrete outcome for their world, grounded in what we've seen in their vertical, not a feature list. Frame from experience and observation, not selling. Close with a **demo-call offer + calendar link** (the sending profile's own link). **Exception: the `vadim` profile has no calendar account, so instead of the demo-call offer + calendar link it closes with a short soft conversational ask (same style as Message 1: "Might be worth a quick chat?"), then the signature. No calendar link.**

#### Structure (in this order)

1. `Hi {first_name},` (a light re-touch is fine; this is a follow-up, keep it natural).
2. **One or two sentences of concrete value** for them / their company: the outcome we help with, tied to their vertical and the campaign hypothesis. This is the core of the message.
3. **Demo-call offer + calendar link** as **plain text** (the sending profile's link, from the table below). Keep the offer short ("Worth 15 min?", "Grab a slot:"). **`vadim` profile only: no calendar link. Replace this with a short soft conversational ask in Message 1 style ("Might be worth a quick chat?", "Open to a quick chat?", "Worth a quick chat to explore?"), then the signature.**
4. **Signature**: first name only.

#### Calendar links (per profile): use the SENDING profile's link

| profile | calendar link |
|---------|---------------|
| katerina | https://meetings.hubspot.com/katerina-galich |
| nick | https://meetings.hubspot.com/nick-omelchak |
| olena | https://meetings.hubspot.com/olena-kudriavtseva |
| katya | https://meetings.hubspot.com/kateryna-boichuk |
| vadim | **none — no calendar account. Use a soft ask instead of the CTA (see below).** |

**`vadim` has no calendar: write his Message 2 WITHOUT the demo-call offer and WITHOUT a calendar link. Instead close with a short soft conversational ask in Message 1 style ("Might be worth a quick chat?"), then the first-name signature (structure step 3).** For every other profile, insert its own link as plain text (no markdown, no shortener); never reuse another person's link, never invent one. If a listed link is ever blank/missing → STOP and ask Vadim.

#### Example (Katerina)
```
Hi Lynn,
Quick follow-up. Where we usually help platforms like yours: members stay engaged longer when they can see real body change between visits, so early GLP-1 drop-off softens. FitXpress adds that from a phone camera, straight into the member profile.
Worth 15 min to walk through it? Grab a slot here: https://meetings.hubspot.com/katerina-galich
Best,
Katerina
```

#### Notes

- Personalize the value line **per contact / vertical**. All numbers / claims come from `proof-points.md`; don't invent stats.
- Don't repeat Message 1 verbatim; this message earns the reply with value, then offers the call.
- Only the follow-up style follows this template; brand no-go rules and product accuracy (FitXpress vs Mobile Tailor) still apply.

## Output format

Write ONE file per batch, `messages/_batch-<batch>.md`, in exactly this shape:

    @@@ <person_id>
    hook: <the specific thing about this person or company the opener stands on>
    proof: <the fact cited, and its source file>
    --- M1
    Hi <first name>,

    <message 1>

    <signature>
    --- M2
    Hi <first name>,

    <message 2>

    <signature>

Then run `scripts/outbound_pack.py split-messages --campaign <slug> --in <that file>`.
It writes the per-person files, counts characters, runs the detector and every ban, and
prints ONLY what failed. Fix those entries in the batch file and run it again. Do not write
per-person files yourself, do not count characters yourself, do not run the detector
yourself.
